t: You're at St. Marylebone Churchyard, a church cemetery in London, and a surprising set of people are buried here. George Stubbs, the self-taught painter best known for his horses, whose Whistlejacket hangs in the National Gallery. James Gibbs, the Scottish architect behind St Martin-in-the-Fields. The Duke of Portland, who was prime minister twice, with a gap of twenty-three years between his terms, the longest of any prime minister. Also here are Lord William Bentinck, the first governor-general of India, the astronomer James Ferguson, and the Italian-born critic Giuseppe Baretti.
